clue.text: Located fashionable fabric

parts.note: something that sat somewhere was located or positioned there
in means in fashion

explanation.surface: Someone has tracked down a trendy material.
explanation.definitionFit: Satin is a smooth glossy woven cloth, one particular kind of textile.

clue.text: Mayoress told off, it's happened before

indicators.note: a dish that has gone off is spoiled, so these letters are out of their proper order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mayor's wife has been reprimanded, and it is not the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Told off' reads naturally as one phrase meaning scolded, but only 'off' is the signal and 'told' belongs to the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a weary idiom said of something tiresomely familiar that keeps recurring.

clue.text: Small child and woman are travelling behind

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: things travelling are on the move, so these letters shift position

parts.note: her is the female pronoun
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mother and toddler are sitting at the back of the bus.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'travelling behind' feels like one phrase, but 'travelling' works only on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Positioned at the back is an adverbial phrase meaning located behind something else.

clue.text: Used for hanging key with small ring on back

indicators.note: going back means the assembled string is read from its far end

parts.note: E is a musical key
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a ring is round, like the letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A key hangs from a little ring on someone's back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' is not a link here: it supplies two letters, and the whole string E, S, O, ON is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is the looped rope with a running knot employed by an executioner on the gallows.

clue.text: Beats back revolutionary's initial success in short bursts

indicators.note: back tells us the word for beats is read from right to left

parts.note: to tan someone is to beat them
Che Guevara is the crossword's standard revolutionary; the 's is possessive

indicators.note: an initial is a first letter, so only the opening of the next word is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of success

explanation.surface: A rebel leader's early triumph comes in fits and starts after he beats off his rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: Snatches are brief fragments or spells, as in snatches of conversation or sleep.

clue.text: Temporary help with stenography

parts.note: temporary means short-lived or short-term
giving a hand is giving help

explanation.surface: An office brings in a temp to help with taking dictation.
explanation.definitionFit: Stenography is the system of rapid writing with abbreviated symbols, which is exactly what this word names.

clue.text: Each movement causes pain

indicators.note: movement suggests the letters are moved around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Every motion you make hurts.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a dull continuous hurt, a synonym for bodily discomfort.

clue.text: Agreed report's to be suppressed

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so we want a word sounding like the one for agreed

parts.note: concurred means agreed

explanation.surface: It is announced that, by consensus, a story will be hushed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' looks like a news story to be suppressed; it is the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebellion that was put down or subdued has been crushed, overcome by force.

clue.text: Flee from Spain after ridiculous duel

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

indicators.note: something ridiculous is absurd and nonsensical, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone runs away from Spain after a farcical sword fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the Spanish letter first: the scrambled fight comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To elude someone is to escape or evade them, getting away from pursuit.

clue.text: Chief bridesmaid, running to 'n' fro after mother, gets praise

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: running suggests the words dash about and their letters end up in a new order

parts.note: the letters as printed, apostrophes ignored
to honour someone is to praise them

explanation.surface: A senior bridesmaid dashes about behind the bride's mother and is complimented for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After mother' puts the mother first in the answer. A married woman in this role takes the title matron rather than maid.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of the principal attendant on a bride when that attendant is already married.

clue.text: Perhaps slip down ahead of man carrying weapon

parts.note: down and under both mean below

indicators.note: a man carrying something holds it inside, so one word sits within another

parts.note: a gent is a man
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: Someone may lose their footing in front of an armed man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slip' feels like a stumble; with 'Perhaps' it is the definition by example. 'Ahead of' puts the first piece before the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a woman's petticoat-style garment worn beneath a dress, an example of underwear.

clue.text: At home let tea include cooked eggs

indicators.note: the preceding words include the solution within them, running across the word breaks

parts.note: the letters sit inside these words, after the h and before the final a

explanation.surface: Someone at home makes a pot of tea and a breakfast to go with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At home' looks like the abbreviation IN, but the solution simply runs through home, let and tea.
explanation.definitionFit: An omelette is a dish of beaten eggs fried in a pan and often folded over a filling.

clue.text: Go to cover drugs with dish

indicators.note: to cover something is to wrap around it, so one piece goes outside the other

parts.note: your go in a game is your turn
E is ecstasy, so two of them make drugs in the plural

explanation.surface: An instruction to hide narcotics under a plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A tureen is a deep lidded serving bowl from which soup is ladled at table.

clue.text: Went back to room that's out of this world

definitions.note: the phrase is adjectival; here it describes the region beyond Earth

indicators.note: going back means the word for went is read from right to left

parts.note: informally, someone who went has relieved themselves, i.e. urinated
room and space both mean available area

explanation.surface: Someone returned to a room that was simply wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went back' reads as returned; 'went' here is the cheeky slang for relieving oneself, reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: The far reaches of the universe lie literally beyond our planet, so the idiom for something amazing describes them exactly.

clue.text: Still shy about start of year with class

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are turned around and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only that is taken

parts.note: the first letter of year

explanation.surface: A pupil remains timid at the beginning of the school year among classmates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Class' suggests a school group, but 'with class' is the definition: elegance.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something elegantly and with flair is doing it in a fashionable, sophisticated manner.

clue.text: With distance to return home, dined on take out

indicators.note: returning means the word for distance is read back the other way

parts.note: a mile is a measure of distance
someone at home is in
to have dined is to have eaten

explanation.surface: Faced with a long trip home, someone eats a takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take out' looks like a takeaway meal; it is the definition, meaning remove. 'On' places the eating after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone out can mean to kill or get rid of them, which is what eliminating does.

clue.text: Aristocrat, briefly following sport, gives money

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: RU is rugby union
a peer is a member of the nobility

explanation.surface: A nobleman who follows a game makes a donation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts the shortened nobleman after the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is the currency unit of India, Pakistan and several other countries.

clue.text: Proper musical makes brief comeback after one that's crude

parts.note: prim means proper and formal
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the shortened title is read backwards
brief means cut short, so the musical's last letter goes

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical

explanation.surface: A respectable stage show returns in a cut-down version after a vulgar one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comeback' sounds like a revival of the show; it is the reversal. 'After one' puts the numeral before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Primitive describes something rough and unsophisticated, simple in construction, just as crude does.

clue.text: Remain with car caught in river

indicators.note: something caught in something else is trapped inside it

parts.note: the Tay is a river in Scotland
RR stands for Rolls-Royce, a car

explanation.surface: Someone stays put after their car has got stuck in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarry is an old-fashioned verb for staying longer, lingering or delaying departure.

clue.text: Getting less flatulence after starting dinner with fish

indicators.note: the starting part of a word is its first letter alone

parts.note: the first letter of dinner
wind is a polite word for flatulence
the ling is a long sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Someone's gas problem eases once dinner and a fish course begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the flatulence after the starting letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwindling describes something steadily diminishing or shrinking in amount.

clue.text: Check girl's included in come back

indicators.note: being included in something means sitting within it

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
Jo is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone verifies that a girl is part of a homecoming.
explanation.definitionFit: To rejoin is to return to a group or place one had left, to go back to it.

clue.text: Judge England/Australia game

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for judge
ENG is the abbreviation for England
A is the international vehicle code for Australia

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to adjudicate an England versus Australia match.
explanation.walkthrough: The slash makes it look like an Ashes fixture; it simply separates two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Jenga is the tabletop block-stacking pastime where players pull wooden pieces from a tower.

clue.text: May hear broadcast, it's more powerful

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard over the air, so we want a sound match

parts.note: may can be replaced by might, and hear stays as it is

explanation.surface: Listeners might catch something on the radio that is stronger.
explanation.walkthrough: The pen is ___ than the sword: the comparative of a word meaning strong.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the comparative form of mighty, meaning having greater strength or power.

clue.text: Stops husband taking keys

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
Alt keys are found on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: A husband picks up the keys and stays put.
explanation.definitionFit: Halts is a verb meaning brings or comes to a standstill, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Amphora still contains wine

indicators.note: the words before it contain the solution within their letters

parts.note: running across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: An ancient storage jar still holds some vino.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white produced in Piedmont, Italy, named after the town.

clue.text: Towards the thin end of the wedge?

definitions.text: Towards the thin end of the wedge?

parts.words: Towards the thin end of the wedge?
parts.note: surface reading: the idiom about a small first step that leads to worse things

parts.words: Towards the thin end of the wedge?
parts.note: setter's reading: a wedge tapers, so its thin end is literally the narrower, lesser part

explanation.walkthrough: The thin end of the wedge is an idiom for a small concession that leads to bigger ones; taken literally it is simply the smaller edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means slightly too small or modest in size, which describes the narrow end of a tapered block.

clue.text: I say flee disorder for a stress-free existence

indicators.note: disorder means a mess, so these letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone urges escape from chaos in favour of a relaxed way of living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disorder' looks like a noun being fled from; it is the signal to rearrange the words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A comfortable, untroubled way of living without hardship or worry is what the phrase describes.

clue.text: Worry about waste

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are turned around and reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone frets over things being thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worry about' reads as one phrase; 'about' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweat over something is an informal idiom for being anxious or fretting about it.
